docs.title: SpMV Benchmark
docs.text:
This project benchmarks Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) on SuiteSparse matrices. It evaluates how graph/ordering structure affects the memory behavior and end-to-end performance of the SpMV kernel.

The benchmark core is written in C. Python is used only for reading result CSVs and generating figures/tables.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
The benchmark is built around a practical question: when does paying the cost of matrix reordering improve SpMV enough to matter?

It records:

  • SpMV runtime and GFLOP/s across measurement methodologies.
  • Reordering cost for RCM, AMD, and ND.
  • Structural matrix metrics such as bandwidth, density, and load imbalance.
  • Cache and TLB counter behavior through PAPI.
  • Cross-platform behavior on x86 and ARM systems.

Why this is memory-focused

SpMV usually performs little arithmetic per byte moved. Performance is often limited by sparse access patterns, cache reuse, TLB behavior, and memory bandwidth rather than floating-point throughput.

docs.title: Main Workflow
docs.text:
Run commands from the project root:

scripts/download_matrices.sh
make all
make run-all
make run-all-tlb
make run-all-cache
make plot

make plot runs the analysis as a module:

python3 -m scripts.analysis

The shortcut script runs the benchmark and plotting pipeline:

scripts/run_all.sh

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Serve these docs locally with:

mkdocs serve -f docs/mkdocs.yml

Build the static docs site with:

mkdocs build -f docs/mkdocs.yml

The documentation uses MkDocs Material. Install the docs dependency with:

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt

docs.title: Analysis Outputs
docs.text:
Python analysis reads benchmark CSV files and writes figures/tables.

Run:

make plot

or directly:

python3 -m scripts.analysis

The module form is intentional: it keeps imports rooted at the project package layout without modifying sys.path inside the script.

docs.title: Data Loading
docs.text:
CSV reading and plotting configuration live in:

utils/data/io.py

The reader expects:

results/x86_results/
results/arm_results/

Both platform result directories must contain the CSVs needed by the analysis.

Mixed platform data

Some plots compare x86 and ARM directly. Those plots require both results/x86_results/ and results/arm_results/ to be populated with compatible matrix sets. If one platform is missing a matrix, the merge step may drop it from cross-platform comparisons.

Missing platform data

The analysis pipeline tolerates missing CSVs. If ARM results are not present yet, x86 plots and tables are still generated while ARM-specific and cross-platform outputs are skipped with warnings.

docs.title: Plot Modules
docs.text:
Plotting code lives under:

utils/plotting/

Module responsibilities:

heatmaps.py : Speedup heatmaps.

barcharts.py : Win/loss summaries and ARM-vs-x86 comparison.

faceted.py : Cache and TLB faceted plots.

sparsity.py : Matrix sparsity pattern plots.

tables.py : LaTeX table generation.

common.py : Shared figure saving helper.

docs.title: Sparsity Plots
docs.text:
Sparsity plotting is not part of the default make plot pipeline because it requires permutation vectors in validation/.

To generate one manually, enable the commented hook in scripts/analysis.py or call the function directly:

from utils.plotting.sparsity import sparse_plot

sparse_plot("matrices/Circuit/nv2.mtx")

The output goes to:

figures/sparsity/

docs.title: Matrices
docs.text: Matrices come from the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection and are stored locally in Matrix Market format.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
The download manifest is:

config/matrix_sources.tsv

It is tab-separated and has this format:

category    output_file.mtx    archive_url    [tar_member]

Fields:

  • category: directory under matrices/, for example FEM or Circuit.
  • output_file.mtx: final Matrix Market filename.
  • archive_url: SuiteSparse .tar.gz URL.
  • tar_member: optional exact .mtx member to extract from the archive.

Blank lines and # comments are ignored.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Run from the project root:

scripts/download_matrices.sh

By default the script reads:

config/matrix_sources.tsv

and writes matrices into:

matrices/

The resulting structure is:

matrices/FEM/inline_1.mtx
matrices/CFD/thermal2.mtx
matrices/Circuit/nv2.mtx
...

docs.title: Custom Manifest
docs.text:
You can pass a custom manifest:

scripts/download_matrices.sh path/to/matrix_sources.tsv

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
MATRIX_ROOT : Override where matrices are written.

MATRIX_ROOT=/tmp/spmv-matrices scripts/download_matrices.sh

FORCE : Overwrite existing .mtx files.

FORCE=1 scripts/download_matrices.sh

docs.title: Extraction Behavior
docs.text:
The downloader:

  1. Creates matrices/<category>/.
  2. Downloads the .tar.gz archive.
  3. Extracts only the requested .mtx file.
  4. Validates that the extracted file starts with %%MatrixMarket.
  5. Skips existing matrices unless FORCE=1 is set.

This keeps archive contents out of the benchmark input tree and leaves only the matrix files that make run-all should discover.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
The benchmark measures how reordering changes SpMV behavior. The central operation is:

y = A * x

where A is stored as CSR and comes from a SuiteSparse Matrix Market file.

docs.title: CSR Execution Model
docs.text:
The parser reads .mtx files into COO and converts them to CSR. CSR is a natural baseline for row-wise SpMV:

for row in rows:
    for idx in row_ptr[row] .. row_ptr[row + 1]:
        y[row] += values[idx] * x[col_idx[idx]]

The expensive part is usually not the multiply-add itself. The irregular access to x[col_idx[idx]] can stress cache and TLB behavior, especially for matrices with wide bandwidth or graph-like sparsity.

docs.title: Reordering Methods
docs.text:
The benchmark compares the original matrix ordering against:

Method Intent RCM Reduce matrix bandwidth and improve locality for some sparse patterns AMD Reduce fill-oriented graph structure; useful as a structural ordering baseline ND Partition graph structure using nested dissection

The reordered matrix is constructed as:

A' = P A P^T

The SpMV input is transformed consistently so correctness is preserved:

y' = A' (P x)
y  = P^T y'

docs.title: Timing Methodologies
docs.text:
The project records three timing variants:

Methodology Purpose RAx Repeated A * x; captures steady-state behavior IOs Swaps input/output vectors between iterations Cold Attempts to reduce warm-cache bias

These methodologies help distinguish real reordering benefits from measurement artifacts caused by cache warmup or reused vector state.

docs.title: Structural Metrics
docs.text:
The main benchmark also records matrix-level properties:

  • number of rows/columns
  • nonzeros
  • average and standard deviation of nonzeros per row
  • maximum and average bandwidth
  • load imbalance estimate
  • density

These metrics make it possible to compare performance against matrix structure, not just against matrix names.

docs.title: Counter Measurements
docs.text:
Two additional binaries measure hardware-counter behavior:

Binary Purpose bin/spmv-benchmark-cache L1/L2/L3 cache miss counters where available bin/spmv-benchmark-tlb DTLB and ITLB miss counters where available

Counter data is collected separately from the timing pipeline because PAPI event availability and overhead differ by platform.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: The project compares x86 and ARM behavior to test whether reordering benefits are architecture-dependent.

docs.title: x86 System
docs.text:
Component Value CPU Intel Core i5-1035G1 Microarchitecture Ice Lake Cores / threads 4 cores / 8 threads L1d 48 KB per core L2 512 KB per core L3 6 MB shared RAM 20 GB Compiler flags -O3 -march=native

The x86 result directory is:

results/x86_results/

docs.title: ARM System
docs.text:
Component Value CPU ARM Neoverse-N1 Microarchitecture Neoverse N1 Cores / threads 4 cores / 4 threads L1d 64 KB per core L2 1 MB per core L3 32 MB shared RAM 16 GB Compiler flags -O3 -mcpu=native

The ARM result directory is:

results/arm_results/

docs.title: Why Compare Architectures?
docs.text:
Reordering changes memory access order, not just arithmetic count. Its value can therefore depend on:

  • cache size and associativity
  • memory latency and bandwidth
  • TLB size and page behavior
  • hardware prefetching
  • OpenMP scheduling overhead

The benchmark keeps the matrix set and generated CSV schema aligned so Python analysis can compare the two platforms directly.

docs.title: Result Figures
docs.text: This page shows representative figures from the thesis output and explains how to read the generated plot groups.

docs.title: Speedup Heatmaps
docs.text:
Generated by:

utils/plotting/heatmaps.py

Output directory:

figures/heatmaps/

Each cell is:

time(original ordering) / time(reordered matrix)

Values above 1.0 indicate a speedup from reordering. Values below 1.0 indicate slowdown.

docs.title: Win/Loss Bar Charts
docs.text:
Generated by:

utils/plotting/barcharts.py

Output directory:

figures/barcharts/

The win/loss plot groups matrices by whether a reordering gives meaningful speedup, neutral behavior, or slowdown under the selected threshold.

docs.title: Cache/TLB Faceted Plots
docs.text:
Generated by:

utils/plotting/faceted.py

Output directory:

figures/faceted/

The faceted plots show one panel per matrix. This avoids hiding matrix-specific effects behind aggregate averages.

docs.title: ARM vs x86 Comparison
docs.text:
Generated by:

utils/plotting/barcharts.py

This chart compares platform behavior using the generated cold-measurement CSVs. It depends on both platform result directories containing compatible matrix names.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Tables are generated as LaTeX files in:

figures/tables/

The table generator produces:

  • scaling tables
  • methodology comparison tables
  • break-even tables
  • matrix characteristics tables

These files are meant to be included directly in the thesis document.

docs.title: Running Benchmarks
docs.text:
Run commands from the project root.

Recommended order

Download matrices first, build all binaries, run the timing benchmarks, then run TLB/cache measurements. Cache and TLB runs use PAPI and are more sensitive to platform permissions and counter availability.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The C benchmark expects:

  • GCC
  • OpenMP
  • CXSparse / SuiteSparse headers and libraries
  • Scotch METIS compatibility library
  • PAPI
  • math library

The Python analysis expects:

  • pandas
  • matplotlib
  • seaborn
  • scipy

The matrix downloader expects:

  • curl or wget
  • tar

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make all

This builds:

bin/spmv-benchmark
bin/spmv-benchmark-perm
bin/spmv-benchmark-cache
bin/spmv-benchmark-tlb

The build also ensures result directories exist:

results/x86_results/
results/arm_results/

docs.title: Run One Matrix
docs.text:
Pass the matrix path relative to matrices/:

make run MTX=FEM/inline_1.mtx

Other single-matrix targets:

make run-cache MTX=FEM/inline_1.mtx
make run-tlb MTX=FEM/inline_1.mtx
make run-perm MTX=FEM/inline_1.mtx

The executable receives FEM/inline_1.mtx, not the full matrices/... path. The C parser prepends the matrices/ root internally.

docs.title: Run All Matrices
docs.text:
The all-matrix targets discover every .mtx under matrices/:

make run-all
make run-all-tlb
make run-all-cache

The full helper script runs all benchmark stages and then analysis:

scripts/run_all.sh

docs.title: Benchmark Stages
docs.text: Stage Make target Output Main timings and metrics make run-all metrics.csv, reorder_times.csv, rax.csv, ios.csv, cold.csv TLB counters make run-all-tlb tlb.csv Cache counters make run-all-cache cache.csv Plots and tables make plot figures/

docs.title: PAPI Notes
docs.text:
Cache and TLB runs use PAPI events. Availability depends on hardware, kernel configuration, and permissions.

Common failure modes:

  • PAPI cannot resolve the requested TLB events.
  • The user does not have permission to access hardware counters.
  • ARM and x86 expose different cache event sets.

The code already uses architecture-specific cache event columns: x86 writes L1, L2, and L3 counters; ARM writes L1 and L2 counters.

docs.title: Result Files
docs.text:
On x86, output is written to:

results/x86_results/

On ARM, output is written to:

results/arm_results/

Expected CSV files:

metrics.csv
reorder_times.csv
rax.csv
ios.csv
cold.csv
cache.csv
tlb.csv

docs.title: Clean
docs.text:
make clean

This removes compiled binaries and CSV result files from the platform result directories. It does not remove downloaded matrices or generated figures.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
The repository is split by responsibility: C benchmark implementation, scripts, matrix metadata, results, and Python analysis utilities.

.
├── config/
│   └── matrix_sources.tsv
├── docs/
│   ├── docs/
│   └── mkdocs.yml
├── figures/
├── include/
├── matrices/
├── results/
│   ├── arm_results/
│   └── x86_results/
├── scripts/
├── src/
├── utils/
│   ├── data/
│   └── plotting/
└── Makefile

docs.title: Important Directories
docs.text:
src/ : C implementation of parsing, CSR/COO conversion, SpMV kernels, reorderings, benchmark execution, timers, and metrics.

include/ : Header files for the C modules.

config/ : Project-level configuration and input metadata. The matrix download manifest lives here as matrix_sources.tsv.

scripts/ : Executable helper scripts. Matrix downloading and full benchmark execution are launched from here.

matrices/ : Downloaded Matrix Market files. The benchmark expects this structure:

matrices/<category>/<matrix>.mtx

results/ : CSV output from benchmark runs. The C code writes into the platform-specific subdirectory:

results/x86_results/
results/arm_results/

utils/data/ : Python data loading and plotting configuration helpers.

utils/plotting/ : Python modules that generate figures and tables. Plot code is split by output type:

utils/plotting/heatmaps.py
utils/plotting/barcharts.py
utils/plotting/faceted.py
utils/plotting/sparsity.py
utils/plotting/tables.py

docs.title: Generated Content
docs.text:
The following directories are generated or regenerated by commands:

  • bin/: compiled benchmark binaries.
  • results/: benchmark CSV output.
  • figures/: Python-generated plots and LaTeX tables.
  • docs/site/: MkDocs static site output.
